title: Behind the Scenes: How Target Prepares for Thanksgiving
summary: Discover how Target's supply chain teams prepare months ahead to deliver Thanksgiving turkeys, appetizers and sides, keeping holiday groceries fresh and ready.
body_markdown:
That turkey you’re preparing for Thanksgiving? It’s at your local Target with help from one of our team’s secret weapons. We call it the “Turkey Push Tool,” a special algorithm that helps us get the meal’s main event to all our stores at the right time. It’s just one piece of our supply chain strategy to reliably deliver the holiday’s familiar favorites and fresh finds to your table as part of our elevated guest experience.


At the heart of our efforts are Target’s nine food distribution centers (FDCs) across the country that focus on ensuring everything is fresh and available for guests. This includes our[$30 Thanksgiving meal for six](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/10/target-brings-more-value-and-delight-to-thanksgiving-with-a-$30-meal-for-six-and-fresh-takes-on-holi) and more than 60 new food and beverage items, with an expanded assortment of $5 sides, pies, appetizers and wine.


The team at our FDC in Rialto, California, which services more than 270 stores, embraces their role in delivering all this newness to busy families for the holiday.


> We’re not just a food distribution center. We’re providing the star of the show. Food is family, food is about memories, and we’re here in the background to make sure that happens.
>
>
> Larry H.
>
>
> Senior Site Director, Target’s FDC in Rialto, California


### Turkey time


To keep food flowing ahead of Thanksgiving, our planning and inventory management teams determine how much to buy, where in our supply chain to store it and when to deliver to our stores.


Take turkeys, for example. Planning begins as early as March, when we make purchasing decisions based on last year's sales, forecasts and product availability. This ensures Target can reserve enough supply from our vendors and get ahead of any issues. Orders then begin arriving at our FDCs in July.


Here’s where the Turkey Push Tool comes in. Developed in partnership with our Target in India team, the algorithm offers visibility into which turkeys each of our 2,000-plus stores need; how many they need; and each store’s unique pick day schedule, which helps teams build an efficient daily shipment plan from our FDCs to our stores. This spreads volume across the supply chain network based on guest demand, balancing product flow and making it manageable for team members — all in service of keeping stores consistently stocked ahead of the holiday.


Since the average turkey moving through our FDCs weighs about 20 pounds, handling the product is also carefully managed. While 75% of our processes are automated, team members do some heavy lifting too, with safety always coming first.


For turkeys, “You have to keep the birds in the power zone,” Larry says. “Make sure you keep it close to your body, use your legs, don't bend at the back.”

### The rest of the meal


An FDC’s core processes seem simple — receive food in bulk from our vendors, store it, break it into cartons and build pallets for trucks to deliver to our stores. At Thanksgiving, these processes scale up as our FDCs handle everything from Good & Gather side dishes and appetizers to new Favorite Day pies to Target exclusives, ingredients and other holiday favorites. Each brings its own demand, shelf life and handling requirements, turning the holiday into a series of overlapping supply chain events stretching out over two months.


“It’s a matter of coordinating space: Every space we have is valuable,” says Larry. “We want to make sure it shows up on time, maintain quality and freshness standards, then get to the stores on time.”

The weeks ahead of Thanksgiving are filled with hustle, bustle and the honking of forklifts. To manage it all, Rialto leaders follow what Larry calls the “CRI” method — chaos, routine and impact.


“We find the chaos, tie it to the routine that controls it, and then make an immediate impact. If we continue to repeat that over and over, the seasons take care of themselves.”


What also helps? Keeping the guest in mind for every carton of food that moves through the FDC. Whether roasting their first turkey or baking Grandma’s sweet potato pie, they’re creating new holiday memories.


> Every carton is a memory that goes on the shelf. When we think about helping all families discover the joy of everyday life, that’s what it’s about.
>
>
> Larry H.
>
>
> Senior Director, Target’s Rialto FDC


### Celebrating a successful season


What makes a successful Thanksgiving season for our supply chain team? Larry says it’s three things: a perfect safety record, seeing Target’s store teams stage the Thanksgiving products and helping guests experience joy.


“You hear about it, you see it on social media and then we feel it as well. When we do those three things, I'm like, ‘You know, I did what I was supposed to. Next holiday.’”
